sources.finding: Jean explicitly states it is free forever with no paid tiers, feature gates or usage limits. Users supply coding-agent subscriptions/API access and their own machines. sources.title: Jean Archive vs delete; Retention and restore; Recovery; Quit confirmation
sources.locator: Archive vs delete; Retention and restore; Recovery; Quit confirmation
sources.finding: Sessions/worktrees can be archived or permanently deleted; archive retention days are configurable and archived work can be restored. Finished unread sessions have a popover. The app documents crash-state persistence/emergency recovery and confirms quitting while runs execute.

sources.title: Jean Context; Commit and sync; Pull request work
sources.locator: Context; Commit and sync; Pull request work
sources.finding: Save/Load Context persists summarized snapshots; Review stores revisitable findings in the Review panel. Magic commands include commit/push, PR creation/update, review, conflict resolution and confirmation before reverting the last local commit. Templates, model/backend/provider and effort defaults can be edited.

sources.title: Jean docs/developer/architecture-guide.md
sources.finding: Architecture guide documents Jean MCP project/worktree/session tools, usage/model controls and commit/PR/review wrappers. Saved secrets are owner-scoped files with optional 24-hour cleanup, not encrypted; all agents share an OS user. GitHub issue polling retries failed starts at most three times and defers rate-limited projects 15 minutes. Native resume/session IDs are persisted for several backends, and run logs retain output for Claude, Kimi and Antigravity.

sources.title: Jean Web Access authentication

sources.finding: Web Access authenticates against one instance token and session cookies. The scoped application has no human membership, named role or enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO implementation. Sharing the instance token does not establish separate human identities.

sources.title: Jean persistent worktree and tracker data
sources.locator: Worktree/ProjectsData schemas; project storage and GitHub/Linear issue integrations; chat Session schema
sources.finding: The native persisted entities are projects, worktrees and chat sessions. Worktrees store labels and external GitHub/Linear identifiers, but no independent product-owned issue lifecycle/catalog is implemented. Repository issue records remain in external trackers.

sources.title: Jean server Docker distribution
sources.finding: Jean publishes a server Docker image that runs jean-server and its coding CLIs inside one container with a persistent /home/jean volume. This is whole-server container deployment, not a separate security sandbox per session.

sources.title: Jean process and workspace isolation

sources.finding: The local runtime runs installed coding CLIs as host processes and separates working files using Git worktrees. It implements no VM isolation allocator. A manually provisioned VM used as the server host is external infrastructure.

Plan, Build and Yolo modes; plan approval dialog offers YOLO, Approve, Approve and clear context, Approve in new worktree or another backend/model. A worktree holds several session tabs.

sources.title: Projects, Worktrees, Sessions
sources.locator: Worktree; Session; Archive vs delete; Labels, recency, and unread work
sources.finding: Worktree metadata includes branch, setup results, PR linkage, issue/PR/security/Linear/Mr. Robot origin, labels and archive state. Sessions keep backend, model, approval state, recap, review results and pending questions; sessions can be forked into a new worktree. Items can be archived or permanently removed.

sources.title: Project Linking
sources.locator: What linking does; How it reaches the backend; Saved contexts across links
sources.finding: Linked projects give sessions read access to the linked directories (passed to Claude CLI via --add-dir plus a system prompt fragment); docs state the agent cannot write to them and writes stay in the active worktree. Saved contexts from linked projects appear in a separate section.

sources.title: Backends, Models, and MCP
sources.locator: Backends; Models and reasoning; Providers; MCP servers
sources.finding: Eight backends with global, project or session defaults; per-session model, thinking or effort level and execution mode. Custom Claude CLI provider profiles change routing. MCP servers are discovered from backend configs and enabled globally, per project or per session.

sources.title: Project Canvas and Chat
sources.locator: Project canvas; Session status at a glance; Running turns and queued prompts; Session debug panel; Command palette
sources.finding: Canvas rolls up worktrees, session cards, git and PR status with filter tabs for Issues, PRs, Mr. Robot and pinned labels, and groups status (waiting for input or approval, planning, executing, review-ready). Codex, OpenCode, PI and Grok steer follow-ups into running turns with auto-steer; others queue editable prompts. Subagent final reports surface in chat. The debug panel shows run logs and token usage and cost breakdowns. Conversation search with Cmd/Ctrl+F.

sources.title: GitHub, Linear, and Reviews
sources.locator: Start from GitHub context; Mr. Robot issue sweeps; Start from Linear; PR review workflows
sources.finding: Sessions start from GitHub issues, PRs, workflow runs, security alerts and advisories, branches or Linear issues. Mr. Robot (beta) periodically checks open issues with label filters and active hours, creates worktrees up to configured run and active-worktree limits, drafts plans and optionally auto-approves them in yolo. Review flows: investigate PR, review changes, address inline PR comments, open/update/merge PR.

sources.title: Magic Commands
sources.locator: Context; Commit and sync; Pull request work; Investigation and release work; Branch work
sources.finding: Save/Load Context, Linked Projects, Create Recap; Commit, Commit & Push, Revert Commit, Pull, Push; Open/Update PR, Review (findings stored in a Review panel), PR Comments, Merge; Investigate Issues/PRs, Generate Release Notes (from a selected GitHub release and merged PRs); Resolve Conflicts.

sources.title: Archive, Recovery, Updates
sources.locator: Archive vs delete; Retention and restore; Unread and orphaned work; Quit confirmation
sources.finding: Sessions and worktrees can be archived or deleted; archive view, restore and retention for a configured number of days. Finished unread sessions appear in a popover. Quitting with running sessions shows a confirmation listing active work.

sources.title: Local-First and Security
sources.locator: Local-first by default; What Jean stores; Credentials and providers; Safe defaults
sources.finding: Core state (projects, worktrees, sessions, preferences, saved contexts) stays on the machine running Jean; Jean uses existing CLI authentication rather than a hosted account. Web Access is off by default, localhost-only, token required.

sources.title: Web Access and Headless
sources.locator: What web access provides; Default behavior; Headless server; Connect from the native app; Security recommendations
sources.finding: Every instance can serve the UI over HTTP/WebSocket with token auth; desktop off by default; jean-server is a Linux headless binary (systemd installer, Docker image). The native app can add a remote and switch its whole backend. Remote access via Tailscale, WireGuard, SSH tunnel or TLS reverse proxy is recommended; token regeneration available in Preferences.

sources.title: What is Jean
sources.finding: Jean is not a hosted coding agent service and not a replacement for source control; users bring their own repository, CLI authentication, git workflow and GitHub/Linear access.

sources.title: Settings and Customization
sources.locator: General; Providers; Usage; Project settings; Experimental features
sources.finding: Auto-steer toggles for Codex, OpenCode, PI and Grok. Providers pane manages custom Claude CLI profiles. Usage pane shows Codex plan type, credits, session and weekly windows. Mr. Robot creates one worktree per issue during active hours. Notification sounds configurable.

sources.title: Opinionated Plugins
sources.finding: Opinionated pane installs third-party tools (RTK, Caveman); they are external projects whose source Jean does not ship.

sources.title: Jean home page
sources.finding: Open source and free forever; connect from a browser or the native app; footer links GitHub and a Discord community (discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q).

sources.finding: Added live tool approvals for Claude, Grok and Kimi including Web Access, in-app sign-in for Claude and Codex MCP servers, a subagent panel and Mr. Robot pause/resume; Codex multi-agent stays on with up to three subagent threads.

sources.title: Jean v1.0.13 release notes
sources.locator: Chat; Agents; Git and integrations; Remote, browser, and terminal; Projects; Magic and MCP; Improvements
sources.finding: Mid-turn steering for Claude via a detached host; automatic continuation after usage limits reset; chat:backend_retry event; queued prompts persist and are editable. Per-agent backend/model/skills, cron routines, memory and named subagent types (Agents). GitLab provider. Persistent SSH tunnel transport, per-client UI state, remote localhost preview via SSH forwards, port picker. Background session alerts, burn pace and reset projections in usage. set_connector and remove_project MCP tools behind approval. PR status and checks shown inline on worktree rows. Named Claude/Codex accounts were added then removed (#852, #875).

sources.title: Jean v1.0.14 release notes
sources.finding: Remote MCP endpoints with browser-free token auth; secret requests via Jean MCP scoped to project or agent and reused by new sessions; opt-in SSH agent forwarding; sessions that delegate through Jean MCP get results back with a Started-by link; sub-sessions grouped under the lead, which can hide them; Review session; command palette searches sessions, messages and settings; canvas grouped by state and compact mobile rows; bulk investigations start one at a time. HttpOnly Web Access cookies. Fixed lost or duplicated prompts on stop/failure, run state mismatch, cancelled runs shown as review; rejected pushes now merge remote commits and retry. Agents closed to new users.

sources.title: Jean v1.0.15 release notes
sources.finding: Mobile Magic favorites, bottom sheets on mobile, iOS status bar and Home Screen fixes; base session permanent for every project; CLIProxyAPI provider added.

sources.title: Jean v1.0.16 release notes
sources.finding: Auto-compact options for Claude, Codex, OpenCode and PI; removed the CLIProxyAPI provider integration.

sources.title: Jean MCP tool catalog
sources.finding: Jean MCP exposes project, worktree (create from GitHub issue/PR, Linear issue or advisory), session (create_session with backend choice, send_chat_message, cancel_session_run, delete_session, read_session_messages, set_session_model), GitHub/Linear issue listing, secrets, commit/push/PR/merge and run_review tools; no tool creates or edits GitHub/Linear issues.

sources.title: Jean MCP dispatch gate
sources.finding: Session-spawning tools are rate limited per source; agent Jean-tool allowlists and read-only subagent blocks apply; the destructive-tool approval gate runs only for Agents sessions. send_chat_message arms chat-to-chat delegation for regular chat callers.

sources.title: Agent approval gate
sources.finding: delete_worktree, push_worktree, merge_pull_request, create_pull_request, remove_project and set_connector wait for user approval only when the caller is an Agents session.

sources.title: Chat-to-chat delegation
sources.finding: A lead chat that sends work to another session through send_chat_message gets the end of that run back as a queued message; outcomes are batched, children needing the user are reported at once, and children are followed in the lead sub-session panel.

sources.title: Jean MCP preferences
sources.finding: Jean MCP is exposed to spawned CLIs by default, with a max recursive spawn depth of 3 and 20 session-spawning calls per minute per source.

sources.title: Mr. Robot settings
sources.finding: Per-project interval, issue limit, max parallel worktrees, included/excluded labels, planning backend/model, optional auto-yolo backend/model and active hours.

sources.title: Mr. Robot scheduler
sources.locator: L167-L172; L441-L458 select_issue_numbers_to_start; L547 start_auto_fix_scheduler; L956-L993
sources.finding: The scheduler runs in jean-core, skips issues already handled or starting, respects the limit and refuses a second concurrent scan; a project is due by interval and active window.

sources.title: Session secrets
sources.finding: Secrets entered on request_secret cards go to owner-only (0600) files under app data, never into chat or model context; scoped to the project (or agent); kept until forgotten or 24 hours; not a security wall because agents run as the same OS user.

sources.title: Web Access browser sessions
sources.finding: A browser exchanges the single access token for an HttpOnly session cookie with 30-day sliding expiry; sessions are bound to the token fingerprint, so regenerating the token signs out every browser; failed attempts are limited per IP. No per-user identity exists.

sources.title: Agents experimental switch
sources.finding: Agents are closed to new users: the Experimental switch only renders for users who already enabled it, and turning it off cannot be undone.

sources.title: Multi-server session list
sources.finding: The native app lists sessions from every online server (local and remote) together.

sources.title: Codex agent threads
sources.finding: Codex sessions are started with agents.max_threads = 3.

sources.title: License
sources.finding: Apache License 2.0 for the repository, which contains the desktop app, jean-core and the headless server.

sources.title: Data persistence guide
sources.finding: App data holds preferences.json, projects.json with three rotating backups and emergency recovery JSON files.

sources.title: Agents database
sources.finding: Agents data is kept in a SQLite database in app data.

sources.title: Push rejection handling
sources.finding: A push rejected as non-fast-forward or fetch-first is detected so Jean can merge the remote and retry.

sources.title: CodeRabbit CLI integration
sources.finding: CodeRabbit CLI is a helper for secondary code review, installable and logged in from General preferences.

sources.title: Web entry
sources.finding: Web UI declares apple-mobile-web-app metadata for Home Screen use; the Tauri config targets desktop only (identifier com.jean.desktop).

sources.title: Jean GitLab issue provider (v1.0.16)
sources.locator: GitLab issue provider and GitLab API helpers
sources.finding: The v1.0.16 GitLab issue provider reads external GitLab issue data through glab and converts it to issue context; this is an external tracker integration, not a native Jean issue catalog.

sources.title: Jean server continuity
sources.locator: Local and remote, in one sidebar; Agents keep running
sources.finding: The home page explicitly says agents on a dedicated server keep running after the controlling laptop closes; jean-server serves the same projects and sessions to browser and native clients.

sources.title: Jean diff viewer (v1.0.16)
sources.locator: GitDiffModal implementation, including the exported component
sources.finding: The v1.0.16 frontend implements GitDiffModal, with diff viewing and file navigation. This pinned implementation supplements the earlier README/release evidence for the review interface.

sources.finding: The guide documents starting a session from Sentry issues when Sentry is configured for the project, alongside GitHub and Linear context.
